articles.summary: This year, America celebrated 250 years since its founding. There were fireworks and parades, but of all the traditions this country has handed down, one of the best may be the one that arrives today: a day set aside, by Abraham Lincoln’s proclamation, to say thank you. This has also been a year in which much has felt uncertain—politically, technologically, economically—and everything seemed to speed up. Maybe that’s why, when we asked our Free Press staff and contributors what they’re grateful for, so many of their answers came back to slowing down and focusing on what’s right in front of us: new babies, a diner that doesn’t deliver, grandparents down the block. The answer comes down to graphics processing units, or GPUs, and how far they’ve come from their humble beginnings as sidekicks to computers’ main chips: central processing units, or CPUs.
